name: Copse-Primeval
specific_features: Automated beacon (distress, navigation, or unknown purpose)
description: Copse-Primeval is a cold, ancient gas giant that has been orbiting its dim red dwarf star since before life arose on most inhabited worlds. Its atmosphere is layered in muted browns and deep blues, the colors of a world that receives little stellar energy and conserves what heat it generates internally. The storm systems are slow and vast, rotating with the ponderous gravity of deep time, their cloud formations unchanged in centuries of observation. A broad debris ring of captured cometary material encircles the equator, its icy fragments catching the dim starlight.

There is an overwhelming sense of age to Copse-Primeval. Its atmospheric patterns have the settled quality of something that reached equilibrium long ago, and the faint reddish light of its star gives the cloud tops a perpetual twilight appearance. The cold is absolute and pervasive, and even the planet's internal heat, which drives the languid storm cycles, barely registers against the background chill of deep space. Probes descending through the atmosphere report methane condensing into lakes on pressure boundaries within the cloud layers, transient surfaces in a world without ground.

An automated navigation beacon orbits Copse-Primeval in a polar trajectory, placed by a colonial survey mission that used the gas giant as a waypoint for expeditions into the surrounding frontier. The beacon is centuries old but still functional, its power source a small radioisotope generator that will outlast most civilizations. Its navigation data is outdated but its presence serves as a marker, a small human artifact in orbit around something vastly older and more patient.

Copse-Primeval's helium-3 reserves are significant but its remote location and dim-star system make extraction economically marginal at current fuel prices. The planet's value lies primarily in its position as a gravitational anchor for transit calculations and as a refueling possibility for expeditions pushing beyond the frontier. As expansion continues outward, Copse-Primeval's significance will grow, transforming from a forgotten waypoint into a critical junction. The beacon continues its patient orbit, waiting for traffic that has not yet arrived.
